newsitem.title: USA: U.S hospital drops embryo researcher - Post.
newsitem.headline: U.S hospital drops embryo researcher - Post.

text.p: The National Institutes of Health has severed its relationship with a researcher who used institutes' equipment and personnel to perform genetic experiments on human embryos, the Washington Post reported on Thursday.
The researcher, Mark Hughes, violated a federal ban on such research with his actions, prompting NIH to sever its ties in October.

An internal NIH investigation concluded that the scientist had used the equipment and federally paid post-doctoral students to perform experiments on human embryos at Suburban Hospital in suburban Bethesda, Md., the Post reported.
The work was approved by the hospital and aimed at detecting genetic defects in test-tube embryos so that only healthy embryos would be implanted into women.
Congress banned federal funding of embryos research in 1995.

The Post quoted Hughes, who is also director of Georgetown University's Institute for Molecular and Human Genetics and whose Georgetown salary was paid in part by NIH, as denying any serious wrongdoing. He said he had a research relationship with NIH, but was never technically a federal employee.
Hughes said his work at Suburban was done free to further his research interests, but he conceded it was a mistake to bring NIH equipment to the lab at Suburban.
Hughes said he believed he had not violated an understanding that no embryo research would be permitted at NIH since the work was done at Suburban on his own time, the Post reported.
